title: Export snapshot checkpoints, row-level redaction and idempotent on-demand exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers have asked for stronger guarantees around scheduled and on-demand CSV/S3 exports: deterministic snapshots for compliance, proof of export for audits, configurable redaction of PII, and reliable idempotent on-demand requests that don't double-charge or duplicate files. Current scheduled export pipeline is optimistic (streaming CDC -> batch) and can produce non-deterministic CSV contents across retries and overlapping runs. This creates problems for compliance-sensitive customers and complicates reconciliation.

Goals:
- Add an explicit export snapshot checkpointing mechanism so each export generation references a monotonic CDC watermark + snapshot id.
- Implement row-level redaction policies that run as a last step before file materialization (configurable per-tenant). Redaction must be reversible for internal audit (via separate encrypted audit artifacts) but irreversible in customer copy.
- Support idempotent on-demand export API with client-supplied idempotency token and server-side deduplication + consistent status polling.
- Provide a "preview" shallow export mode that streams first N rows for customer validation without producing final artifact.
- Ensure compatibility with S3/CSV scheduled exports and webhook-driven delivery (send manifest + manifest-signature).

Non-goals:
- Full redesign of the CDC ingestion pipeline. We will build checkpointing and snapshot logic on top of the existing CDC stream.

Success metrics:
- 99.9% of exports produce identical manifest+checksum across retry cycle.
- On-demand duplicate artifact rate <0.1% after rollout.
- End-to-end latency for on-demand snapshot generation (1 hour window) under SLO of 15m for small tenants (<100k rows) and 60m for large tenants.
- Audit artifact availability for 100% of exports for 90 days.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Each export (scheduled or on-demand) is assigned snapshot_id and cdc_watermark; both are included in manifest and UI.
2) Exports are resumable: if a job fails mid-run, re-run uses the same snapshot_id and resumes based on progress markers; final CSV identical to successful run.
3) Row-level redaction rules can be configured per-tenant via Console and applied deterministically (examples: mask-email, hash-cc-last4, redact-ssn).
4) On-demand API accepts idempotency_token and returns existing artifact if token seen within retention window.
5) Preview endpoint streams first N rows without creating final CSV object.
6) Manifests include HMAC signature (using tenant KMS key) to allow customers to verify integrity when receiving via webhook.

High-level design:
- Snapshot coordinator service (new) orchestrates start of export and records snapshot metadata: snapshot_id, start_watermark, end_watermark, tenant_id, redaction_profile, export_mode (scheduled/on-demand/preview), idempotency_token if provided. Stored in durable export_metadata table.
- Export workers consume CDC with a per-snapshot window filter (apply start_watermark..end_watermark). Workers write partitioned CSV shards to a temporary bucket/prefix and emit progress markers to metadata.
- Finalizer job collects shards, applies deterministic row-level redaction (idempotent by using fixed salts per-tenant stored in KMS-wrapped metadata), concatenates shards in stable key order, computes manifest (sha256 checksum + row count), signs manifest with tenant-specific key and writes final objects to tenant S3 destination.
- Idempotency: export_metadata keyed by (tenant_id, idempotency_token). For on-demand calls, we first check for an existing, non-expired snapshot and return it. If not present, we create a new snapshot and set a lease to avoid double-starts.
- Preview mode: workers stream first N rows through a lightweight path that omits full concatenation and manifest signing; previews are ephemeral and not stored as final artifacts.

Implementation tasks (owner tags):
- API: add POST /v1/exports/on_demand with idempotency_token and preview flag (Luca)
- Snapshot coordinator service + export_metadata schema (Luca)
- Export worker: windowed CDC filtering and temp shard writes (Ravi)
- Redaction library and deterministic salts + KMS integration (Priya)
- Finalizer: stable ordering concat, manifest generation + signing (Ravi)
- S3 delivery + webhook manifest delivery with signature header (Luca)
- UI: Console export history shows snapshot_id, watermark, preview links and redaction profile (Emma)
- E2E test harness for simulating failures, retries and validating idempotency (QA)

Monitoring & observability:
- Metrics: exports.started, exports.completed, exports.failed, exports.duplicate_detected, preview.requests, redaction.errors.
- Traces: end-to-end trace from API call -> snapshot coordinator -> worker -> finalizer.
- Alerts: elevated export.failed rate >0.5% queue length > threshold.

Rollout plan:
1) Launch coordinator + metadata in staging and run backfill on a subset of tenants.
2) Enable preview mode for 10 pilot customers.
3) Gradually route scheduled exports through snapshot flow (start with low-traffic tenants).
4) After 2 weeks of stability and automated checks, flip on idempotency enforcement for on-demand API.

Security & compliance notes:
- Redaction keys and deterministic salts stored wrapped in customer KMS (or Redwood-managed KMS if customer opts out) and are only accessible to finalizer with proper IAM.
- Manifest HMAC uses tenant key material; webhook consumers will receive X-Export-Manifest-Signature header.
- Audit artifacts (unencrypted pre-redaction traces) are stored in an encrypted auditing bucket for 90 days and access-controlled to SRE/compliance.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should preview use the same deterministic redaction as final exports? (Current plan: yes for consistency.)
- Retention window for idempotency tokens (defaults to 7 days) — ops trade-off between memory and user expectation.
- Whether to support multi-tenant shards parallelization for very large tenants or constrain concurrency per-tenant to preserve ordering guarantees.

Next steps:
- Spike to implement snapshot coordinator prototype and end-to-end minimal pipeline for a single tenant (Ravi + Priya)
- Security review for KMS usage and audit artifact retention (security team)
- UX mockups for Console preview and export history (Emma)
